problem: Map-based ObjectNav methods such as SemExp regress a long-term goal anywhere on the map, and classical frontier exploration ignores semantics. Neither exploits both frontiers and semantic priors, so exploration in large unknown scenes is inefficient.
motivation: Visual target navigation is a prerequisite for high-level robot tasks, and robots must generalize to unseen scenes without a ground-truth map. Frontiers give a small set of valid, reachable exploration candidates. Semantic map features tell which candidate is likely to lead to the target.
key_idea: Learn a PPO policy that selects one of 4 candidate frontier cells as the long-term goal, using semantic and frontier map features plus the goal category, with invalid action masking to handle a variable number of frontiers.
insight: Restricting the global action space to frontiers and feeding the frontier map to the policy both matter. Removing the frontier map from the input drops HM3D success from 0.538 to 0.470, and replacing the learned policy with a goal-agnostic closest-frontier sampler drops it to 0.465. With GT semantic segmentation, success rises to 0.640, so perception quality is a major bottleneck. Multi-floor scenes in HM3D are also a failure source for the 2D map.
method: Semantic map: builds a K×M×M top-down map (obstacle, explored, Cn semantic channels) from RGB-D via a point cloud projection, with RedNet segmentation. Stairs are removed from the obstacle map and the old floor is cleared on floor change.

Frontier map: extracts explored edges from the explored map, subtracts the dilated obstacle map, clusters the frontier cells, and removes small clusters. Cost-utility scoring (λ_CU=0.5) keeps the top 4 cells, one per channel of a 4×M×M map.

Frontier semantic policy (global): PPO with the semantic and frontier maps (K+4 channels) cropped around the agent, a 5-layer conv net with an FC layer giving 2048-d features, plus a goal word embedding. It picks one of 4 frontier channels. The goal is updated every 25 steps.

Invalid action masking: masks the frontier channels that are empty when fewer than 4 frontiers exist, so they are never sampled and the policy gradient is unaffected. The centroid of the chosen cluster becomes the long-term goal.
Local policy: If the target is visible in the semantic map, its cells become the goal. Otherwise, FMM plans a path to the long-term goal and outputs discrete actions.
Reward shaping: sum of a dense geodesic-distance-decrease reward, a smooth-coverage exploration reward (Σ A_i/√n_i), and a time penalty of -0.001.

setting.backbone: PPO global policy (5-layer conv + FC, 2048-d) with RedNet semantic segmentation; FMM local planner
setting.training_data: Habitat Gibson tiny (25 train scenes) and HM3D (75 train scenes); about 2M frames of RL training on one V100; RedNet fine-tuned as in Ye et al.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 480×640 + odometry pose + goal category
setting.action_space: global: 1 of 4 frontier cells as long-term goal; low-level: forward 25 cm, turn ±30°, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson, HM3D); real-world Jackal robot demo
setting.privileged: none (GT semantics used only in the ablation)

numbers.extra: success radius 0.1 m, max 500 steps; 5 val scenes of Gibson tiny

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.715) in the paper. Success (SR) and SPL are reported as the printed fractions rather than percentages. Gibson has no canonical benchmark name in the list.
results: FSE reaches 0.715 success / 0.360 SPL on Gibson and 0.538 / 0.246 on HM3D, beating SemExp (0.652 / 0.336 on Gibson; 0.379 / 0.188 on HM3D). On HM3D, SemExp's DTG (2.943) is lower than FSE's (3.745). The real-world Jackal demo works without much fine-tuning.
limitations: Semantic segmentation errors are a major bottleneck: GT segmentation adds about 10% success and SPL.
The 2D map struggles in multi-floor HM3D scenes, and the real-world demo is qualitative only, with noisy depth and localization.
The policy is limited to 4 candidate frontiers, and the success threshold of 0.1 m is nonstandard, which limits comparability with other results.
